reason: I want to start the vibration route: the picture shows the eardrums stretched across the ends of the ear canals.
expectation: I expect the eardrums to fit at the ends of the canals, ready to pass vibrations inward.

alternatives.reason: The hearing cells also appear to belong in the inner ear, but I chose to start with the outer route.

effect: The eardrum now sits at the end of the canal, so I can continue the inward route.
reason: The picture shows the middle-ear bones linking the eardrum toward the inner ear.
expectation: I expect the bones to connect to the eardrum and pass its vibrations inward.

alternatives.reason: Building the sensing tissue is also a goal, but I want to continue the vibration route first.

effect: The bones carry movement from the eardrum toward the fluid-filled inner ear, completing the first goal.
reaction: The movement arrows made the route clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it builds the inner ear's sensing tissue.
expectation: I expect the hearing cells to fit into the fluid-filled chambers; I'm not yet sure exactly how their hairs detect movement.

effect: Fluid movement bends the sensory hairs and changes signals at their nerve connections; the next goal is to join the hearing nerves.
reaction: The inset helped explain how movement becomes a nerve signal, though not the detailed mechanism.
reason: The hearing pathways lead from the sensing cells toward the brain, matching the new goal.
expectation: I expect the inner ears to connect to the hearing pathways so their signals can travel toward the brain.

alternatives.reason: Joining the sound-conducting and sensing parts also makes sense, but I chose to connect the nerves first.

effect: The sensing tissue now connects to nerve fibres leading toward the brain; the outer sound-conducting parts still need joining.
reaction: The outlined outer parts make the remaining connection clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it joins the vibration route to the sensing tissue and nerves.
expectation: I expect a complete route from the ear canal through the inner ear to the hearing pathways.

effect: The completed ears show the full route from moving air through vibrations to nerve signals toward the brain; all goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate routes come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the hearing cells was most worthwhile: the inset showed fluid movement bending their hairs and changing nerve signals.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the eardrums to the canals was straightforward but less interesting than seeing how vibrations become signals.

surprise.text: I hadn't understood how the tiny hairs were involved until the fluid movement and bending were shown.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals made the connections understandable, although the menu supplied compatible pairs.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter: seeing separate parts join into a working sensory route was interesting, though the early fittings felt predictable.
